# dog

**dog** is a command-line DNS client, like `dig`.

It has colourful output, understands normal command-line argument syntax, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.

![A screenshot of dog making a DNS request](dog-screenshot.png)

## Examples

    dog example.net                          Query a domain using default settings
    dog example.net MX                       ...looking up MX records instead
    dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1              ...using a specific nameserver instead
    dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T           ...using TCP rather than UDP
    dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T   As above, but using explicit arguments

## Command-line options

### Query options

    <arguments>              Human-readable host names, nameservers, types, or classes
    -q, --query=HOST         Host name or domain name to query
    -t, --type=TYPE          Type of the DNS record being queried (A, MX, NS...)
    -n, --nameserver=ADDR    Address of the nameserver to send packets to
    --class=CLASS            Network class of the DNS record being queried (IN, CH, HS)

### Sending options

    --edns=SETTING           Whether to OPT in to EDNS (disable, hide, show)
    --txid=NUMBER            Set the transaction ID to a specific value
    -Z=TWEAKS                Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks

### Protocol options

    -U, --udp                Use the DNS protocol over UDP
    -T, --tcp                Use the DNS protocol over TCP
    -S, --tls                Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol
    -H, --https              Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol

### Output options

    -1, --short              Short mode: display nothing but the first result
    -J, --json               Display the output as JSON
    --color, --colour=WHEN   When to colourise the output (always, automatic, never)
    --seconds                Do not format durations, display them as seconds
    --time                   Print how long the response took to arrive

## Installation

Binary downloads of dog are available from the releases section on GitHub for 64-bit Windows, macOS, and Linux targets. They contain the compiled executable, the manual page, and shell completions.

Package manager installations may also be available:
- For Arch Linux: `dog` package
- For Homebrew on macOS: `dog` formula  
- For NixOS: `dogdns` package

## Documentation

For detailed documentation on how to use dog, see the manual page or visit: <https://dns.lookup.dog/>

## License

dog's source code is licenced under the European Union Public Licence.

% dog(1) v0.1.0

<!-- This is the dog(1) man page, written in Markdown. -->
<!-- To generate the roff version, run `just man`, -->
<!-- and the man page will appear in the ‘target’ directory. -->


NAME
====

dog — a command-line DNS client


SYNOPSIS
========

`dog [options] [domains...]`

**dog** is a command-line DNS client.
It has colourful output, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.


EXAMPLES
========

`dog example.net`
: Query the `A` record of a domain using default settings

`dog example.net MX`
: ...looking up `MX` records instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1`
: ...using a specific nameserver instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T`
: ...using TCP rather than UDP

`dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T`
: As above, but using explicit arguments


QUERY OPTIONS
=============

`-q`, `--query=HOST`
: Host name or domain name to query.

`-t`, `--type=TYPE`
: Type of the DNS record being queried (`A`, `MX`, `NS`...)

`-n`, `--nameserver=ADDR`
: Address of the nameserver to send packets to.

`--class=CLASS`
: Network class of the DNS record being queried (`IN`, `CH`, `HS`)

By default, dog will request A records using the system default resolver. At least one domain name must be passed — dog will not automatically query the root nameservers.

Query options passed in using a command-line option, such as ‘`--query lookup.dog`’ or ‘`--type MX`’, or as plain arguments, such as ‘`lookup.dog`’ or ‘`MX`’. dog will make an intelligent guess as to what plain arguments mean (`MX` is quite clearly a type), which makes it easier to compose ad-hoc queries quickly. If precision is desired, use the long-form options.

If more than one domain, type, nameserver, or class is specified, dog will perform one query for each combination, and display the combined results in a table. For example, passing three type arguments and two domain name arguments will send six requests.

DNS traditionally uses port 53 for both TCP and UDP. To use a resolver with a different port, include the port number after a colon (`:`) in the nameserver address.


SENDING OPTIONS
===============

`--edns=SETTING`
: Whether to opt in to DNS. This can be ‘`disable`’, ‘`hide`’, or ‘`show`’.

`--txid=NUMBER`
: Set the transaction ID to a specific value.

`-Z=TWEAKS`
: Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks.


TRANSPORT OPTIONS
=================

`-U`, `--udp`
: Use the DNS protocol over UDP.

`-T`, `--tcp`
: Use the DNS protocol over TCP.

`-S`, `--tls`
: Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol.

`-H`, `--https`
: Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol.

By default, dog will use the UDP protocol, automatically re-sending the request using TCP if the response indicates that the message is too large for UDP. Passing `--udp` will only use UDP and will fail in this case; passing `--tcp` will use TCP by default.

The DNS-over-TLS (DoT) and DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) protocols are available with the `--tls` and `--https` options. Bear in mind that the system default resolver is unlikely to respond to requests using these protocols.

Note that if a hostname or domain name is given as a nameserver, rather than an IP address, the resolution of that host is performed by the operating system, _not_ by dog.

Unlike the others, the HTTPS transport type requires an entire URL, complete with protocol, domain name, and path.


OUTPUT OPTIONS
==============

`-1`, `--short`
: Short mode: display nothing but the first result.

`-J`, `--json`
: Display the output as JSON.

`--color`, `--colour=WHEN`
: When to colourise the output. This can be ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’, or ‘`never`’.

`--seconds`
: Do not format durations as hours and minutes; instead, display them as seconds.

`--time`
: Print how long the response took to arrive.


META OPTIONS
============

`--help`
: Displays an overview of the command-line options.

`--version`
: Displays the version of dog being invoked.


ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
=====================

dog responds to the following environment variables:

## `DOG_DEBUG`

Set this to any non-empty value to have dog emit debugging information to standard error. For more in-depth output, set this to the exact string ‘`trace`’.


RECORD TYPES
============

dog understands and can interpret the following record types:

`A`
: IPv4 addresses

`AAAA`
: IPv6 addresses

`CAA`
: permitted certificate authorities

`CNAME`
: canonical domain aliases

`HINFO`
: system information and, sometimes, forbidden request explanations

`LOC`
: location information

`MX`
: e-mail server addresses

`NAPTR`
: DDDS rules

`NS`
: domain name servers

`OPT`
: extensions to the DNS protocol

`PTR`
: pointers to canonical names, usually for reverse lookups

`SOA`
: administrative information about zones

`SRV`
: IP addresses with port numbers

`SSHFP`
: SSH key fingerprints

`TLSA`
: TLS certificates, public keys, and hashes

`TXT`

When a response DNS packet contains a record of one of these known types, dog will display it in a table containing the type name and a human-readable summary of its contents.

Records with a type number that does not map to any known record type will still be displayed. As they cannot be interpreted, their contents will be displayed as a series of numbers instead.

dog also contains a list of record type names that it knows the type number of, but is not able to interpret, such as `IXFR` or `ANY` or `AFSDB`. These are acceptable as command-line arguments, meaning you can send an AFSDB request with ‘`dog AFSDB`’. However, their response contents will still be displayed as numbers. The `-Z` command-line argument can be used one or more times to set some protocol-level options in the DNS queries that get sent. It accepts the following values:

`aa`

`ad`

# Note: This works for both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and also PowerShell 7 (Core).
# But beware that in Windows PowerShell 5.1, it has issues with completing args if they start with '-'.
# For more information about the bug, see: https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/2912
# In PowerShell 7+, it should work correctly.
Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName 'dog' -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)

    [string]$argsString = $commandAst.ToString()

    # skip the "dog", split the args afterwards as array
    [string[]]$argsArray = $argsString.Split([char[]]@(' ', '=')) | Select-Object -Skip 1
    if ($argsArray -eq $null) { $argsArray = @() }

    # detect if starting a new arg (aka ending with space and asking for a completion)
    [bool]$isNewArg = $cursorPosition -gt $argsString.Length
    if ($isNewArg) {
        # if writing a new arg, add empty arg so that current and previous would be shifted
        $argsArray += ''
    }

    # get current arg (empty if starting new)
    [string]$currentArg = $argsArray[-1]
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($currentArg)) {
        $currentArg = ''
    }

    # get previous arg
    [string]$previousArg = $argsArray[-2]
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($previousArg)) {
        $previousArg = ''
    }

    [string[]]$dnsTypeValues = @('A', 'AAAA', 'CAA', 'CNAME', 'HINFO', 'MX', 'NS', 'PTR', 'SOA', 'SRV', 'TXT')

    [string[]]$completions = @()
    [bool]$isOptionValue = $argsString.EndsWith('=')

    # complete option value
    switch -Regex ($previousArg) {
        '^(-q|--query)'       { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(-t|--type)'        { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += $dnsTypeValues }
        '^(-n|--nameserver)'  { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(--class)'          { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('IN', 'CH', 'HS') }
        '^(--edns)'           { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('disable', 'hide', 'show') }
        '^(--txid)'           { $isOptionValue = $true }
        '^(-Z)'               { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('aa', 'ad', 'bufsize=', 'cd') }
        '^(--color|--colour)' { $isOptionValue = $true; $completions += @('always', 'automatic', 'never') }
    }

    # detect whether to complete option value
    if ($isOptionValue) {
        if (!$isNewArg) {
            # if using =, complete including the option name and =
            $completions = $completions | ForEach-Object { "$previousArg=$_" }
        }
    } 
    else {
        # if not completing option value, offer DNS type values first
        $completions += $dnsTypeValues

        # complete option name
        [string[]]$allOptions = @(
            '-q', '--query',
            '-t', '--type',
            '-n', '--nameserver',
            '--class',
            '--edns',
            '--txid',
            '-Z',
            '-U', '--udp',
            '-T', '--tcp',
            '-S', '--tls',
            '-H', '--https',
            '-1', '--short',
            '-J', '--json',
            '--color', '--colour',
            '--seconds',
            '--time',
            '-?', '--help',
            '-v', '--version'
        ) | Sort-Object

        $completions += $allOptions
    }

    if ($completions.Count -gt 0) {
        # narrow down completions by like* matching
        return $completions -like "$currentArg*"
    }
}

def enc_name(name):
    out=b''
    for part in name.rstrip('.').split('.'):
        if part: out += bytes([len(part)])+part.encode()
    return out+b'\x00'

def rdata(name, typ, val):
    # val spec strings
    if typ==1: return socket.inet_aton(val)
    if typ==28: return socket.inet_pton(socket.AF_INET6,val)
    if typ in (2,5,12): return enc_name(val)
    if typ==6:  # SOA mname rname serial refresh retry expire minimum

    if typ==33:
        pri,wt,port,tgt=val.split(' ',3); return struct.pack('!HHH',int(pri),int(wt),int(port))+enc_name(tgt)

import socket,os,struct,sys
PORT=int(os.environ.get('PORT','5353'))
def enc(n):
    out=b''
    for p in n.rstrip('.').split('.'):
        if p: out+=bytes([len(p)])+p.encode()
    return out+b'\x00'
n=int(os.environ.get('NRECS','10'))
u=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM);u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET,socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1);u.bind(('127.0.0.1',PORT))
t=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_STREAM);t.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET,socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1);t.bind(('127.0.0.1',PORT));t.listen(5)
import threading
def tcp():
    while True:
        c,a=t.accept()
        h=c.recv(2);l=struct.unpack('!H',h)[0];d=b''
        while len(d)<l: d+=c.recv(l-len(d))
        resp=build(d)
        c.sendall(struct.pack('!H',len(resp))+resp)
def build(data):
    tid,flags,qd,an,ns,ar=struct.unpack('!HHHHHH',data[:12])
    i=12
    while data[i]!=0: i+=1+data[i]
    i+=5
    an=b''
    for k in range(n):
        an+=enc('a%d.example.net.'%k)+struct.pack('!HHIH',1,1,300,4)+bytes([1,2,3,4])
    return struct.pack('!HHHHHH',tid,flags,1,n,0,0)+data[12:]+an
threading.Thread(target=tcp,daemon=True).start()
while True:
    d,a=u.recvfrom(4096)
    resp=build(d)
    print('UDP resp size',len(resp),file=sys.stderr)
    u.sendto(resp,a)
EOF
cd /workspace && for n in 1 5 30 100 200; do kill $(cat /tmp/t/pid 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.2; XENV="NRECS=$n" setsid nohup python3 /tmp/t/big.py >/tmp/t/big.log 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/t/pid; sleep 0.5; printf "N=%-4s auto: " $n; timeout 5 ./executable -n 127.0.0.1:5353 example.net 2>&1 | head -2 | tr '\n' '|'; echo " TCPQ=$(grep -c TCPQ /tmp/t/big.log 2>/dev/null) UDPSZ=$(grep -c 'UDP resp' /tmp/t/big.log 2>/dev/null)"; done; kill $(cat /tmp/t/pid) 2>/dev/null"}

import socket,os,struct,sys,time
PORT=int(os.environ.get('PORT','5353'))
D=float(os.environ.get('DELAY','2.5'))
u=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM);u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET,socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1);u.bind(('127.0.0.1',PORT))
def enc(n):
    out=b''
    for p in n.rstrip('.').split('.'):
        if p: out+=bytes([len(p)])+p.encode()
    return out+b'\x00'
while True:
    d,a=u.recvfrom(4096)
    time.sleep(D)
    tid,flags,qd,an,ns,ar=struct.unpack('!HHHHHH',d[:12])
    i=12
    while d[i]!=0: i+=1+d[i]
    i+=5
    an=enc('d.example.net.')+struct.pack('!HHIH',1,1,300,4)+bytes([1,2,3,4])
    resp=struct.pack('!HHHHHH',tid,flags,1,1,0,0)+d[12:i]+an
    u.sendto(resp,a)
EOF

import socket,os,struct,sys,time
PORT=int(os.environ.get('PORT','5353'))
D=float(os.environ.get('DELAY','2.5'))
u=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM);u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET,socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1);u.bind(('127.0.0.1',PORT))
def enc(n):
    out=b''
    for p in n.rstrip('.').split('.'):
        if p: out+=bytes([len(p)])+p.encode()
    return out+b'\x00'
while True:
    d,a=u.recvfrom(4096)
    time.sleep(D)
    tid,flags,qd,an,ns,ar=struct.unpack('!HHHHHH',d[:12])
    i=12
    while d[i]!=0: i+=1+d[i]
    i+=5
    an=enc('d.example.net.')+struct.pack('!HHIH',1,1,300,4)+bytes([1,2,3,4])
    resp=struct.pack('!HHHHHH',tid,flags,1,1,0,0)+d[12:i]+an
    u.sendto(resp,a)
EOF
cd /workspace && for delay in 0.5 2.5 65.5 3700; do kill -9 $(cat /tmp/t/pid 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.2; nohup env PORT=5353 DELAY=$delay python3 /tmp/t/delay.py >/tmp/t/s3.log 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/t/pid; sleep 0.4; printf "delay=%-6s " $delay; timeout 20 ./executable --time -n 127.0.0.1:5353 example.net 2>&1 | tail -1; done

 [bytes([0xC3,0xA9]), b'e'],

 [bytes([0x7E,0x7F]), b'e'],

]

p.terminate()
PY

cd /tmp/tc && openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key_ext.pem -out cert_ext.pem -days 3650 -nodes -subj "/CN=localhost" -addext "subjectAltName=IP:127.0.0.1" 2>/dev/null; openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key_fn.pem -out cert_fn.pem -days 3650 -nodes -subj "/CN=localhost" -addext "subjectAltName=IP:127.0.0.1,1.2.3.4.5=critical,ASN1:UTF8:test" 2>/dev/null; openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key_p.pem -out cert_p.pem -days 3650 -nodes -subj "/CN=localhost" -addext "subjectAltName=IP:127.0.0.1" 2>/dev/null; python3 -c "
import base64,re
d=open('cert_p.pem').read()
b=base64.b64decode(''.join(re.findall(r'-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n(.*)-----END CERTIFICATE-----',d,re.S)[0].split()))
b=bytearray(b); b[60]^=0x01  # tamper
open('cert_tampered.pem','wb').write(b)
"; openssl x509 -in cert_tampered.pem -inform DER -out tampered.pem 2>&1|head -2; ls -l cert_fn.pem tampered.pem 2>/dev/null | head

    arcsec=milli/1000.0
    if abs(arcsec)>324000: return 'Out of range'
    deg=int(abs(arcsec)//3600); rem=abs(arcsec)-deg*3600

{"command": "cd /workspace && cat > /tmp/t/opt.py <<'PY'
import json,os,subprocess,time,struct
def run(recs_a, recs_add, port=5355, args=[]):
    env=dict(os.environ); env['PORT']=str(port); env['SPECS_A']=json.dumps(recs_a); env['SPECS_ADD']=json.dumps(recs_add)
    p=subprocess.Popen(['python3','/tmp/t/dns.py'],stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,env=env)

    p2=subprocess.run(['./executable']+args+['--edns=show','--color=never','-n','127.0.0.1:%d'%port,'example.net'],capture_output=True)
    p.terminate(); return ('rc=%d\n%s'%(p2.returncode,p2.stdout.decode('utf8','replace')))
def opt(cls,ttl,data): return [41,"0x"+data.hex() if isinstance(data,bytes) else data, cls, ttl]

cd /workspace && cat > /tmp/t/rectype.py <<'PY'
import json,os,subprocess,time
env=dict(os.environ); env['PORT']='5357'
p=subprocess.Popen(['python3','/tmp/t/dns.py'],stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,env=env)
open('/tmp/t/pid','w').write(str(p.pid)); time.sleep(0.8)
types=[17,18,23,25,35,36,37,43,46,47,50,51,53,55,61,62,249,251,252,254,32769,32770,63,64,65,74,56,57,58,3,7,14,19,20,21,22,26,30,31,32,34,38,39,40,48,49,66,99]
for t in types:
    env['SPECS_A']=json.dumps([[t,"hello",1,300]])
    p.terminate(); time.sleep(0.2)
    p=subprocess.Popen(['python3','/tmp/t/dns.py'],stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,env=env)
    time.sleep(0.4)
    p2=subprocess.run(['./executable','-J','-n','127.0.0.1:5357','example.net'],capture_output=True,text=True)
    o=p2.stdout.strip()
    try:
        d=json.loads(o.split('\n')[0])
        if d['responses'] and d['responses'][0]['answers']:
            a=d['responses'][0]['answers'][0]
            print('type %-6s -> %s %s'%(t,a['type'],json.dumps(a['data'])))
        else:
            print('type %-6s -> (no answers) %s'%(t,(p2.stderr.strip().split('\n')[0] or 'EMPTY')))
    except Exception: print('type %-6s -> ERR %s'%(t,(p2.stderr.strip().split('\n')[0] or 'EMPTY')))
p.terminate()
PY
python3 /tmp/t/rectype.py

import socket,os,struct,sys
PORT=5357
NAMES=os.environ.get('NAMES','example.net.').split(',')
RT=int(os.environ.get('RT','17'))
RD=bytes(os.environ.get('RD','hello'),'utf8')
def enc(n):
    out=b''
    for p in n.rstrip('.').split('.'):
        if p: out+=bytes([len(p)])+p.encode()
    return out+b'\x00'
u=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM);u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET,socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1);u.bind(('127.0.0.1',PORT))
print('ready',file=sys.stderr)
while True:
    d,a=u.recvfrom(4096)
    tid,flags,qd,an,ns,ar=struct.unpack('!HHHHHH',d[:12])
    i=12
    while d[i]!=0: i+=1+d[i]
    i+=5
    an=b''
    for nm in NAMES:
        nm=nm.strip()
        an+=enc(nm)+struct.pack('!HHIH',RT,1,300,len(RD))+RD
    resp=struct.pack('!HHHHHH',tid,flags,1,len(NAMES),0,0)+d[12:i]+an
    u.sendto(resp,a)
EOF

cd /workspace && cat > /tmp/t/nm.py <<'EOF'
import socket,os,struct,sys
PORT=5357
NAMES=os.environ.get('NAMES','example.net.').split(',')
RT=int(os.environ.get('RT','17'))
RD=bytes(os.environ.get('RD','hello'),'utf8')
def enc(n):
    out=b''
    for p in n.rstrip('.').split('.'):
        if p: out+=bytes([len(p)])+p.encode()
    return out+b'\x00'
u=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM);u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET,socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1);u.bind(('127.0.0.1',PORT))
print('ready',file=sys.stderr)
while True:
    d,a=u.recvfrom(4096)
    tid,flags,qd,an,ns,ar=struct.unpack('!HHHHHH',d[:12])
    i=12
    while d[i]!=0: i+=1+d[i]
    i+=5
    an=b''
    for nm in NAMES:
        nm=nm.strip()
        an+=enc(nm)+struct.pack('!HHIH',RT,1,300,len(RD))+RD
    resp=struct.pack('!HHHHHH',tid,flags,1,len(NAMES),0,0)+d[12:i]+an
    u.sendto(resp,a)
EOF
kill -9 $(cat /tmp/t/pid 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.3; nohup env PORT=5357 NAMES="example.net." RT=17 RD="hello" python3 /tmp/t/nm.py >/tmp/t/sa.log 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/t/pid; sleep 0.5
echo "=== same name, type 17, 5 bytes"; timeout 3 ./executable -n 127.0.0.1:5357 example.net 2>&1 | head -2
kill -9 $(cat /tmp/t/pid) 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.3; nohup env PORT=5357 NAMES="example.net." RT=17 RD="abcd" python3 /tmp/t/nm.py >/tmp/t/sa.log 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/t/pid; sleep 0.5
echo "=== same name, type 17, 4 bytes"; timeout 3 ./executable -n 127.0.0.1:5357 example.net 2>&1 | head -2
kill -9 $(cat /tmp/t/pid) 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.3; nohup env PORT=5357 NAMES="other.net." RT=17 RD="abcd" python3 /tmp/t/nm.py >/tmp/t/sa.log 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/t/pid; sleep 0.5
echo "=== diff name, type 17, 4 bytes"; timeout 3 ./executable -n 127.0.0.1:5357 example.net 2>&1 | head -2

cd /workspace && cat > /tmp/t/httpsrv4.py <<'EOF'
import socket,ssl,os,struct,sys,time
PORT=443
MODE=os.environ.get('MODE','2headers')
def enc(n):
    out=b''
    for p in n.rstrip('.').split('.'):
        if p: out+=bytes([len(p)])+p.encode()
    return out+b'\x00'
ctx=ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER); ctx.load_cert_chain('/tmp/t/cert.pem','/tmp/t/key.pem')
s=socket.socket();s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET,socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1);s.bind(('127.0.0.1',PORT));s.listen(5)
print('ready',MODE,file=sys.stderr)
def dns_body(buf):
    idx=buf.find(bytes([0x01,0x00,0x00,0x01]))
    start=idx-2
    tid,flags,qd,an,ns,ar=struct.unpack('!HHHHHH',buf[start:start+12])
    i=start+12
    while buf[i]!=0: i+=1+buf[i]
    i+=5
    anr=enc('d.example.net.')+struct.pack('!HHIH',1,1,300,4)+bytes([9,9,9,9])
    return struct.pack('!HHHHHH',tid,flags,1,1,0,0)+buf[start+12:i]+anr
while True:
    c,a=s.accept()
    try: tls=ctx.wrap_socket(c,server_side=True)
    except Exception as e: print('hs fail',repr(e),file=sys.stderr);c.close();continue
    tls.settimeout(3); buf=b''
    try:
        for _ in range(5):
            d=tls.recv(65535)
            if not d: break
            buf+=d
            if b'\r\n\r\n' in buf: break
    except Exception: pass
    body=dns_body(buf)
    if MODE=='2headers':
        resp=b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/dns-message\r\nX-Foo: bar\r\nContent-Length: '+str(len(body)).encode()+b'\r\n\r\n'+body
    elif MODE=='nohead':
        resp=b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n'+body
    elif MODE=='chunked':
        resp=b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n'+hex(len(body))[2:].encode()+b'\r\n'+body+b'\r\n0\r\n\r\n'
    elif MODE=='extra':
        resp=b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: '+str(len(body)).encode()+b'\r\n\r\n'+body+b'EXTRA'
    else:
        resp=b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: '+str(len(body)).encode()+b'\r\n\r\n'+body
    tls.sendall(resp); print('sent',file=sys.stderr)
    tls.close()
EOF
for m in 2headers nohead chunked extra; do echo "=== $m"; kill -9 $(cat /tmp/t/pid 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.3; nohup env PORT=443 MODE=$m python3 /tmp/t/httpsrv4.py >/tmp/t/sd.log 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/t/pid; sleep 0.6; SSL_CERT_FILE=/tmp/t/cert.pem DOG_DEBUG=trace timeout 6 ./executable -H -n https://127.0.0.1/ example.net 2>&1 | sed -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -E "dns_transport::https" | head -8; done

    /// Read a length-prefixed DNS message back over TLS.
    pub fn receive(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error> {
        log::info("dns_transport::tcp", "Waiting to receive...");
        let mut header = [0u8; 2];
        ssl_read_exact(self.ssl, &mut header)?;
        let len = u16::from_be_bytes(header) as usize;
        let mut buffer = vec![0u8; len];
        let mut pos = 0usize;
        while pos < len {
            let n = ssl_read(self.ssl, &mut buffer[pos..])?;
            pos += n;
        }
        log::info(
            "dns_transport::tcp",
            &format!("Received {} bytes of data", pos + 2),
        );
        log::debug("dns_transport::tcp", "We have enough bytes");
        Ok(buffer)

import json,os,subprocess,time,sys,struct
def enc(n):
    out=b''
    for p in n.rstrip('.').split('.'):
        if p: out+=bytes([len(p)])+p.encode()
    return out+b'\x00'
def hdr(tid=0x1234,flags=0x8400,qd=1,an=0,ns=0,ar=0):
    return struct.pack('!HHHHHH',tid,flags,qd,an,ns,ar)
Q=enc('example.net')+struct.pack('!HH',1,1)
def full(rest,an=1,ns=0,ar=0,flags=0x8400,qd=1,q=Q):
    return hdr(flags=flags,qd=qd,an=an,ns=ns,ar=ar)+q+rest
def rec(nm,typ,cls,ttl,data): return nm+struct.pack('!HHIH',typ,cls,ttl,len(data))+data
def run(hexdata, port=5396, args=[]):
    env=dict(os.environ); env['PORT']=str(port); env['RAW']=hexdata
    p=subprocess.Popen(['python3','/tmp/t/dns.py'],stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,env=env)
    open('/tmp/t/pid','w').write(str(p.pid)); time.sleep(0.5)
    a=subprocess.run(['timeout','4','/tmp/t/mine']+args+['-n','127.0.0.1:%d'%port,'example.net'],capture_output=True)
    b=subprocess.run(['timeout','4','./executable']+args+['-n','127.0.0.1:%d'%port,'example.net'],capture_output=True)
    p.terminate()
    return (a.returncode,a.stdout,a.stderr,b.returncode,b.stdout,b.stderr)

# dog (reverse-engineered reimplementation)

This workspace contains a from-scratch reimplementation of the `dog` command-line
DNS client, written by observing the behaviour of the provided `./executable`
binary and the bundled documentation (README, man page, shell completions).

## Layout

```
Cargo.toml            cargo workspace; three crates
dog/                  the binary (`dog`)
  src/main.rs         entry point, request loop, error/exit-code handling
  src/options.rs      command-line parsing + dog's Debug output of its options
  src/hints.rs        /etc/hosts lookup used for the "also exists in hosts" warning
  src/sysconf.rs      /etc/resolv.conf parsing (system default nameserver)
  src/output.rs       text table / JSON / short output
  src/text.rs         dog's exact help and version text (generated from the binary)
dns/                  the DNS protocol library dog uses
  src/wire.rs         packet building and parsing
  src/records.rs      record types, their text and JSON forms
  src/name.rs         domain names, IDNA handling, wire errors
  src/punycode.rs     RFC 3492 punycode
  src/tables.rs       generated Unicode tables (folding, NFKC, composition)
dns-transport/        transports
  src/udp.rs src/tcp.rs src/tls.rs src/https.rs src/ossl.rs
compile.sh            builds `./executable` with cargo (release, panic=abort)
```

## What was verified as matching

Compared byte-for-byte against the provided binary (`/tmp/t/cmp.sh`, plus the
python harnesses used during development):

* `--help`, `--version`, no-arguments behaviour (help on stdout, exit 3)
* all observed option-parse error messages and exit code 3, including
  duplicate-option detection, `--` handling, combined short flags, `-Z` tweaks,
  `--txid`, `--edns`, `--class`, `--type` (names and numbers), invalid domains
* DNS-over-UDP and DNS-over-TCP transports
* text table layout (column widths, right/left alignment, colours per record
  type, section markers `A`/`+`), `Status:` lines, TTL formatting, `--seconds`
* JSON output (`responses` array, per-record `data` shapes, `duration`)
* short mode (`-1`) including the "No results" exit status 2
* record contents: A, AAAA, CNAME, NS, PTR, SOA, MX, TXT, HINFO, SRV, SSHFP,
  TLSA, CAA, LOC (dog parses NAPTR/29 as LOC), OPT, and unknown types
* malformed-packet error messages and exit code 1
* TLS/HTTPS nameserver panics, reproduced at the same source locations
  (`dns-transport/src/tls.rs` line 41 col 65 in the built tree, matching the
  binary's reported position) and the same messages
* HTTPS HTTP/1.1 request format and response-body handling
* `DOG_DEBUG` / `DOG_DEBUG=trace` log lines and their colour escapes

## Known gaps / differences

* TLS error strings come from the system OpenSSL (3.0.2) whereas dog reports
  OpenSSL 1.1.1-style strings. Certificate-verification failures are formatted
  the way dog does (the common cases are tabulated in
  `dns-transport/src/ossl.rs`), but other OpenSSL failures (protocol version
  mismatch alerts, for instance) will not be byte-identical.
* IDNA support covers the BMP up to U+2FFF; characters dog rejects as
  "unassigned" outside that range would be accepted here.
* dog's TCP transport spins forever when a response is truncated mid-body; this
  implementation reproduces that (matching dog), which means such a test would
  hang for both binaries.
* `dog -H` with the system resolver produces dog's "You must pass a URL...".
  error; TLS with the system resolver uses the first resolv.conf entry, which
  could not be verified against dog here because both nameservers in the
  container's resolv.conf are unreachable.
* dog's UDP transport appears to accept datagrams larger than its EDNS payload
  size; the read buffer here is 64 KiB.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "dog: reverse-engineered reimplementation" 2>&1 | tail -2; git log --oneline | head -3; git status --short | head -5"}
